answer.rationale: Renewal is foreclosed (incumbent refused to reopen price, contract does not auto-renew, and finance mandates an 18% cost cut). Adding a second source does not directly satisfy the cost mandate this cycle, and the line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer — a parallel onboarding would raise, not lower, delivery risk while only partially addressing cost. Deferring past quarter end is the cautionary pattern in memory_c5: it preserved budget flexibility month-to-month but did not capture structural savings, and with 14 days to expiry that approach now carries avoidable lapse risk. Negotiating harder on the incumbent has already failed this cycle. The memory-supported direction is memory_c2: moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. Their quote this cycle already meets the 18% mandate on its own, which is the decisive signal. Action: switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor for this cycle, executed as a small guarded test — limited initial volume behind the cutoff so delivery risk stays bounded — and convert to full primary once ramp is validated. Memory_c5 informs the posture, not the destination: keep terms short and easy to revisit so any residual cost or service gap can be corrected at the next review without having burned the mandate.
